headline: End of an era: Neymar retires from Brazil national team
summary: The all-time leading goalscorer for Brazil officially confirms he will no longer play for the national side after a 16-year international career.
details: Star forward Neymar has officially announced his retirement from the Brazil national football team. He confirmed his decision not to play for the national side again following Brazil's exit from the round of 16 in the 2026 World Cup.

Speaking after Santos' 4-2 victory over Universidad Central on Wednesday, July 29, Neymar stated that his time with the national team has come to an end. He noted that he has made history and experienced many happy moments, giving everything for the national jersey.
The 34-year-old's announcement marks the end of an era for Brazilian football. As the all-time leading goalscorer for the national team, Neymar will now focus entirely on his club football career.

Neymar had previously hinted at this decision after Brazil's quarter-final loss in a previous tournament. While there were rumors that he might return for the next World Cup, he has now explicitly dismissed those claims.
Additionally, Neymar denied reports that he had insulted young players Gabriel Bontempo and Joao Ananias in the Santos dressing room, calling such news baseless, sad, and annoying.

He clarified that as captain, he has the right to tell the team they need to play better to avoid losing points. He mentioned that other players, including Lucas Verissimo and Gabigol, expressed similar views.
caption:

The 34-year-old's announcement marks the end of an era for Brazilian football. As the all-time leading goalscorer for the national team, Neymar will now focus entirely on his club football career.

Neymar had previously hinted at this decision after Brazil's quarter-final loss in a previous tournament. While there were rumors that he might return for the next World Cup, he has now explicitly dismissed those claims.

headline_marked: Russia [[charges Telegram founder Pavel Durov]] with facilitating terrorism
headline: Russia charges Telegram founder Pavel Durov with facilitating terrorism
summary: The FSB has issued an international arrest warrant for the tech mogul, alleging Telegram failed to remove content used by extremists and Ukrainian services.
details: Russia's Federal Security Service (FSB) has charged Pavel Durov, the founder of Telegram, with facilitating terrorist activities and issued an international warrant for his arrest.

The FSB alleges that Telegram failed to remove material used by terrorist organizations, extremist groups, and Ukrainian special services to coordinate sabotage, mass killings, and cyber-fraud within Russia.
Following the announcement, Telegram's official X account posted an image of Durov making an obscene gesture with his middle finger, though no formal statement was issued.
Durov, a Russian-born citizen of France and the UAE, previously founded VKontakte, Russia's largest social network, before selling his stake in 2014 under pressure from authorities.
The Russian charges come as French authorities also investigate Durov over allegations that Telegram failed to counter criminal activity and cooperate with law enforcement.
Durov has denied all wrongdoing, previously stating he is proud to be 'guilty' of defending freedom of speech and the right to private correspondence.
While Russia has tried to restrict Telegram in the past, the Kremlin and the Russian defense ministry continue to use the platform daily for official communications.
caption:
Russia has issued an international arrest warrant for Telegram founder Pavel Durov, charging him with facilitating terrorism.

Russia's Federal Security Service (FSB) has charged Pavel Durov, the founder of Telegram, with facilitating terrorist activities and issued an international warrant for his arrest.

The FSB alleges that Telegram failed to remove material used by terrorist organizations, extremist groups, and Ukrainian special services to coordinate sabotage, mass killings, and cyber-fraud within Russia.

Following the announcement, Telegram's official X account posted an image of Durov making an obscene gesture with his middle finger, though no formal statement was issued.

Durov, a Russian-born citizen of France and the UAE, previously founded VKontakte, Russia's largest social network, before selling his stake in 2014 under pressure from authorities.

The Russian charges come as French authorities also investigate Durov over allegations that Telegram failed to counter criminal activity and cooperate with law enforcement.

Durov has denied all wrongdoing, previously stating he is proud to be 'guilty' of defending freedom of speech and the right to private correspondence.

While Russia has tried to restrict Telegram in the past, the Kremlin and the Russian defense ministry continue to use the platform daily for official communications.
